MARINE NATIONALE — SURFACE FLEET AUDIT (faction key `fra`, surface hulls only; the submarines belong to the other two workflows).

SCOPE MEASURED: 27 French hulls with layer:"sea" — 23 era rows in js/eras.js (e50→e00) and 4 hand-written e20 rows in js/rules.js. Everything resolved under jsc after generations.js, never read off the source line.

THE HEADLINE, AND IT IS THE SAME DEFECT AS THE OHIO AND THE IFVs. Measured: 18 of the 23 era hulls fire a borrowed AMERICAN weapon id (`w_e**_nato_<role>`); the other five are patrol boats carrying the generic `hmg`. Not one French era hull carried a single French-designed naval weapon. The borrowings are not near-misses:

  De Grasse (1956), an ANTI-AIRCRAFT cruiser with sixteen 127 mm/54 Mle 1948, fires
    "Nine 203mm/55 Mk 16 rapid-fire guns in three turrets" — that is USS Des Moines.
  Colbert (1959), the same kind of ship, fires "Terrier and Talos SAM launchers" —
    two United States Navy systems France never bought, and with tgt.air = 0, so a
    weapon whose NAME is "SAM launchers" cannot engage an aircraft.
  Suffren (1967), whose own desc says "built around Masurca, a French area
    air-defence missile", fires an American 127 mm Mk 42 and cannot shoot at air.
  The A69 aviso (1976) fires "Mk 13 launcher for SM-1MR and Harpoon" — an Oliver
    Hazard Perry. The A69 never had a SAM, a Harpoon or a Mk 13 in its life.
  Cassard (1988), an ANTI-AIR frigate, fires "90-96 cell Mk 41 VLS with
    SM-2/ESSM/Tomahawk" — an Arleigh Burke — with tgt.air = 0. France has never put
    a Mk 41 cell or a Tomahawk on a surface ship in any decade.
  Horizon (2010) fires a "Mk 45 Mod 4 127mm". Horizon has no 127 mm gun at all.
  FREMM Aquitaine (2012) fires "One 57mm Mk 110" — the Bofors on an American LCS.
  Clemenceau, Foch and Charles de Gaulle all carry "Mk 15 Phalanx CIWS". France has
    never bought Phalanx, Goalkeeper or RAM for any hull in this roster.

THE SIX DEFECT CLASSES, ANSWERED.

1. LAND ATTACK. The real answer for France is narrow and interesting, and the game had none of it. By gun: throughout, and the big-gun ships had a lot of it (De Grasse and Colbert each had sixteen 127 mm). By missile: NOTHING until MM40 Exocet Block 3 in 2008 gave the round GPS waypoints and a coastal secondary mode, and nothing proper until MdCN — qualified 2015, operational 2017, first fired in anger on 14 April 2018 when Aquitaine, Languedoc and Auvergne put rounds into Syrian chemical-weapons sites. MdCN is the only ship-launched land-attack cruise missile any European navy has. MEASURED: there is no MdCN weapon anywhere in WEAPONS (zero entries matching /mdcn|scalp|naval cruise/), and the e20 FREMM's own desc names it — "the naval cruise missile MdCN, which no other European escort carries" — exactly the Ohio/Tomahawk defect on the one ship in Europe that genuinely has the capability. Conversely MM38 (1975) and MM40 Block 2 (1993) were ANTI-SHIP ONLY and must not carry ground:1.

2. DESCRIPTION VERSUS LOADOUT. Nine rows. The purest is fra_e80_cruiser, whose name IS "Colbert (Exocet)" and whose full name IS "Colbert (C611) after the Exocet fit" — and which carries no Exocet. Then Le Corse ("57 mm mountings" → American 76 mm Mk 33), Cdt Rivière ("three 100 mm, a 305 mm ASW mortar" → one American 127 mm, no ASW), T 47 Surcouf ("six 127 mm in three twin turrets" → "Three 127mm/54 Mk 42 single mounts"), Suffren (Masurca), the A69 ("four MM38 Exocet"), Tourville ("a towed array and Malafon"), Le Fougueux ("depth charges aft" on a submarine chaser with sub:0), FREMM and Horizon (Aster, Exocet, MdCN, VDS — none present).

3. ANACHRONISM. All 23 era rows carry a `service` field and every one matches the class's real commissioning — I checked the rows that have the field and confirmed the four e20 rows that do NOT have one are all ships in service today (POM 2023, FREMM 2012, Horizon 2010, CdG 2001), so the gap is the e20 convention, not an oversight. Two real finds: La Combattante (P730, 1964, 202 t, one 40 mm and two 20 mm) carries a "heavyweight torpedo" of 340 damage she never had; and fra_e80_carrier's service date 1986 is silently overwritten to 1961 by a duplicate key later in the same object literal.

4. WRONG IDENTITY. Eight weapons belonging to another navy, listed above. Plus the duplicate-key trap: fra_e80_carrier declares Foch (R99) / 1986 / ASMP and then, INSIDE THE SAME BRACES, restates name, full, service and desc as Clemenceau (R98) / 1961. The later key wins, so half the row is dead text nobody will ever see and two competing histories sit in one line.

5. AREA AIR DEFENCE — the single most important distinction after 1980, and the game could not make it anywhere in the French line. MEASURED before the fix: 13 of 27 French sea hulls could engage an aircraft at all, and NOT ONE of the three ships France built around an area SAM could: Suffren and Colbert with Masurca (in service 1968, the first area missile France built rather than bought) and Cassard with forty SM-1MR on a Mk 13. Meanwhile La Fayette, a genuine point-defence escort with eight Crotale rounds, had the same air capability as a Horizon: none. After the fix, 21 of 27 engage air, and Masurca / SM-1MR / Aster 30 sit at 9.8 / 10.4 / 14.8 tiles while Crotale and Sadral sit at 6.2 and 4.4 — the ladder is now visible.

6. CAPABILITY GAPS. ASW was a hole: MEASURED, exactly one of 27 French surface hulls had a weapon with sub:1, and it was La Combattante's phantom torpedo. France's ASW record is one of the strongest things about this navy — the 305 mm Mle 1954 mortar, the L5 from 1971, MU90, and above all Malafon (1965–1997), a rocket-boosted glider that flies 13 km and drops an L4 torpedo at the far end, which neither the Royal Navy nor the Bundesmarine had an answer to. Anti-ship was a hole too: MEASURED, zero of the 23 era hulls carried Exocet — the weapon of 1982 and the one France sold to seven navies — although MM38 was on the A69s, Tourville, Georges Leygues, Colbert and Suffren from 1975.

WHAT THE GAME ALREADY HAS RIGHT, and it is a lot. The three hand-written e20 hulls are correct and well-judged: FREMM with 76 mm + Aster 15 + Exocet, Horizon with 76 mm + Aster 30 + Exocet, Charles de Gaulle with Aster 15 and nothing else (which is exactly her real SAM fit). The deliberate emptinesses are all correct and the comments say why: no `missileboat` in any era, because France built La Combattante by the dozen for export and never commissioned one; no `cruiser` from e90, because Colbert paid off on 24 May 1991; no `ssgn`, because MdCN goes in a Suffren SSN's torpedo room. The NAVGUN table's refusal to carry a `fra` row is right for the stated reason — an era-less override would have bolted a 1953 gun onto a 2012 FREMM — and its comment already prescribes the fix I have written. The patrol-boat line is right end to end, dates and framing both. La Fayette's rcs 0.14 is right and is the point of the ship.

REALISM OVER SYMMETRY. I have invented nothing to fill a slot. MdCN gets sea:0 because unlike a TASM-era Tomahawk it has no anti-ship mode and never had one. MM38 and MM40 Block 2 get ground:0 because no Exocet before Block 3 could be told to fly to a map reference ashore. France gets no Phalanx, no Harpoon, no Mk 41 and no Tomahawk in any era, because it never bought any of them.

findings.unit: the whole French surface fleet, all eras
findings.whatTheGameHas: MEASURED: exactly one of 27 French surface hulls has a weapon with tgt.sub = 1, and it is La Combattante's phantom torpedo. Sonar ratings up to 9.0 sit on ships with nothing to shoot.
findings.whatIsReal: France's anti-submarine record is one of the strongest things about this navy: the 305 mm Mle 1954 four-barrel mortar on Le Corse, Commandant Riviere and the T 47s; Malafon (1965-1997), a rocket-boosted glider that flies 13 km and drops an L4 torpedo at the far end, which no other navy in this roster had an equivalent to; the L5 Mod 4 from 1971; MU90 today; and the Tourville/Georges Leygues towed arrays and the FREMM's CAPTAS-4.
findings.fix: New weapons asw_mortier305, asw_malafon, asw_l5; reuse the existing asw_mu90 and depthchg (both currently orphaned or near-orphaned). After the fix 7 of 27 hulls can prosecute a submarine, which is the right shape — cruisers and carriers still cannot.

findings.unit: the whole French surface fleet, e80 through e00
findings.whatTheGameHas: MEASURED: zero of the 23 era hulls carry Exocet. Only the three hand-written e20 hulls do.
findings.whatIsReal: MM38 Exocet was operational in 1975 and was fitted to the A69 avisos, the Tourville class, the Georges Leygues, Colbert and the Suffrens. MM40 Block 2 (72 km) arrives 1993 on La Fayette and Cassard. Exocet is the anti-ship weapon of this navy and the one that mattered in 1982 — and the reason seven navies bought French-designed hulls.
findings.fix: New ssm_exocet38 (1975, 42 km) and ssm_exocet40b2 (1993, 72 km), BOTH with tgt.ground = 0 because neither generation could attack a target ashore. The existing ssm_exocet keeps ground:1 because it is Block 3 (2008), which can.

findings.whatTheGameHas: MEASURED: no weapon anywhere in WEAPONS matches /mdcn|scalp|naval cruise/. corvette_f's desc names "the naval cruise missile MdCN, which no other European escort carries" and the loadout has no such round.
findings.whatIsReal: MdCN — Missile de Croisiere Naval, a navalised SCALP with a booster — was qualified in 2015, declared operational in 2017, and first fired in anger on 14 April 2018 (Operation Hamilton) when Aquitaine, Languedoc and Auvergne put rounds into Syrian chemical-weapons sites. Range about 1,000 km, sixteen in Sylver A70 cells on the eight FREMM ASM hulls. It is the only ship-launched land-attack cruise missile any European navy has, and it has no anti-ship mode.
findings.fix: New weapon `mdcn` with tgt {ground:1,air:0,sea:0,sub:0} and manual:true, added to corvette_f and fra_e00_corvette. This is the single most important fact about the modern French surface fleet and the game did not have it.

findings.whatTheGameHas: The object literal declares name "Clemenceau (ASMP)", full "Foch (R99) with Super Etendard and ASMP", service "1986" and a desc about the AN 52 and ASMP — and then, INSIDE THE SAME BRACES, restates "name":"Clemenceau CV", "full":"Clemenceau (R98) with Super Etendard and ASMP", "service":"1961" and a different desc. The later keys win. Resolved under jsc the row is Clemenceau R98 / 1961.
findings.whatIsReal: The surviving half is the coherent one — fra_e90_carrier is already Foch (R99), so letting the dead half win would have put Foch in both decades. But the discarded half carries the fact that justifies an e80 carrier row at all: ASMP at sea from 1986, which made France the only navy besides the United States with nuclear strike off a carrier deck. Two competing histories in one line, one silently thrown away, is a maintenance hazard whichever half is right.
findings.fix: Promote the winning values into the row's own fields and delete the duplicate key block. Verified under jsc: resolved name, full, service, desc and weapons are byte-identical before and after, so this is purely a readability fix.

findings.whatTheGameHas: weapons: ["hmg"] — a 12.7 mm with tgt {g1,a0,s1,u0}. sonar 2.2. The full name is "Le Fougueux-class patrouilleur (submarine chaser)" and the desc says "A 40 mm forward, depth charges aft".
findings.whatIsReal: Fourteen 325-tonne submarine chasers built in French yards under US Offshore Procurement, 1954-57: one 40 mm Bofors, 20 mm, Hedgehog and depth charges. The whole purpose of the type is a capability the unit cannot exercise — it is a submarine chaser with sub:0.
findings.fix: weapons: ["hmg","depthchg"]. depthchg already exists in rules.js and is currently carried by nothing.

findings.whatTheGameHas: "Two twin 76mm/50 Mk 33" — the American mount — while the desc says "a raked bow and 57 mm mountings". No ASW weapon despite sonar 3.8 on a first-rate escort.
findings.whatIsReal: Four E50 Le Corse and fourteen E52 Le Normand: six 57 mm/60 ACAD Mle 1951 in three twin mounts, a 305 mm Mle 1954 anti-submarine mortar, and twelve 550 mm ASW torpedo tubes. The first postwar class drawn and built entirely in France, which is exactly what the desc says and exactly what the loadout denies.
findings.fix: weapons: ["navgun_57","asw_mortier305"]. navgun_57 already exists ("57mm naval gun", tgt g1,a1,s1).

findings.whatTheGameHas: "One 127mm/54 Mk 42" — American — and no ASW weapon, while the desc says "three 100 mm, a 305 mm ASW mortar, and space for eighty troops".
findings.whatIsReal: Nine aviso-escorteurs: three 100 mm Mle 1953 in single automatic turrets, two 30 mm, one 305 mm Mle 1954 mortar, six 550 mm ASW tubes. Four hulls later traded a 100 mm for four MM38 Exocet.
findings.fix: weapons: ["navgun_100_fr","asw_mortier305"].

findings.whatTheGameHas: "Three 127mm/54 Mk 42 single mounts", tgt {g1,a0,s1,u0}, while the desc says "six 127 mm in three twin turrets".
findings.whatIsReal: Twelve escorteurs d'escadre with six 127 mm/54 Mle 1948 in three TWIN turrets — a French gun, not the American Mk 42 — plus six 57 mm/60 and twelve 550 mm tubes. Both gun calibres were dual-purpose, so air:0 is wrong as well. The Tartar conversions are 1962-65 and the Malafon ASW conversions 1968-71, both outside the e50 window, so the as-built fit is the right one for this row.
findings.fix: weapons: ["navgun_127_mle48","navgun_57"].

findings.kind: area air defence flattened across the whole line
findings.whatTheGameHas: MEASURED baseline: 13 of 27 French sea hulls can engage an aircraft at all, and not one of the three ships France built around an AREA air-defence missile can — Suffren and Colbert (Masurca) and Cassard (SM-1MR) all resolve to tgt.air = 0. So an area-defence ship, a point-defence escort and a gun frigate were indistinguishable everywhere in the French line.
findings.whatIsReal: The French air-defence ladder is sharp and datable: Masurca from 1968 (Suffren 1967, Duquesne 1970; Colbert from the 1970-72 refit; gone with Suffren 2001 and Duquesne 2008), Crotale EDIR point defence from 1979 (Tourville, Georges Leygues, every La Fayette), SM-1MR on Cassard 1988, Sadral Mistral from 1990, Aster 15 and Aster 30 under PAAMS from 2008. That ladder is the most important thing about a French escort after 1980.
findings.fix: New sam_masurca (range 9.8, reload 9.5 — area reach, 1960s rate of fire), sam_crotale_nav (6.2, point defence), sam_sadral (4.4, last ditch); reuse sam_sm1, sam_aster15, sam_aster30. After the fix 21 of 27 hulls engage air and the ladder is legible.

findings.whatTheGameHas: weapons: ["hmg","torpedo"] — "heavyweight torpedo", 340 damage, tgt {g0,a0,s1,u1}. This is a submarine weapon.
findings.whatIsReal: One prototype fast patrol boat of 202 tonnes with one 40 mm Bofors and two 20 mm, able to lay mines, with no torpedo tubes at all. Its importance is as a design: the La Combattante II and III that grew out of it were sold to Greece, Germany, Iran, Libya, Malaysia, Nigeria and Qatar, and the German Type 148 Tiger is one of them — which the desc already says well.
findings.fix: weapons: ["hmg"]. (gbr_e60_patrol, deu_e50_patrol and deu_e60_patrol carry the same phantom torpedo; those are other workflows' rows and I have not touched them.)

findings.unit: fra_e80_aswhelo and fra_e90_aswhelo — Westland Lynx HAS Mk4 (FN), 1979 and 1994
findings.whatTheGameHas: Both carry asw_mk54, "Mk 54 lightweight torpedo".
findings.whatIsReal: The Mk 54 is American and entered service in 2004. The French Lynx carried the Mk 46 and the French L4/L5. These are layer:"air" units and so strictly outside a surface-fleet brief, but they are the surface fleet's only anti-submarine aircraft for two decades and asw_mu90 and the proposed asw_l5 are both to hand. Flagging, not fixing, to avoid colliding with whoever owns the air roster.
findings.fix: Consider asw_l5 for both, or leave to the air-roster owner.

findings.unit: Georges Leygues (F70 ASM) — absent from every era
findings.whatTheGameHas: No hull. The class is named in two descs — "The Georges Leygues class that follows them from 1979 is the ship most people think of" and "the seven Georges Leygues ... is the more numerous and more useful ship" — and never fielded, while the three-hull Tourville holds e80 and the two-hull Cassard holds e90.
findings.whatIsReal: Seven Georges Leygues, commissioned 1979-1990: two 100 mm, four to eight MM40 Exocet, Crotale EDIR, two Lynx, DUBV-23 hull sonar and DUBV-43 variable depth. The most numerous major French escort of the period by a wide margin.
findings.fix: No edit proposed. The roster has one destroyer slot per faction per era, so this is a choice the descs already explain and defend. Recording it so the owner knows it was examined.

findings.whatTheGameHas: Both carry "Air wing of ~90 aircraft" (the shared w_e50/e60_nato_carrier).
findings.whatIsReal: Arromanches, an ex-Colossus light fleet carrier, operated about 24 aircraft; Clemenceau about 40. Ninety is a Forrestal.
findings.fix: No edit proposed: these ids are shared with the American and British carrier rows, so correcting the text would move two other factions' hulls and is outside a France-only mandate. Flagging for whoever owns the shared naval weapon table.

findings.whatTheGameHas: FREMM: 76 mm + Aster 15 + Exocet Block 3. Horizon: 76 mm + Aster 30 + Exocet Block 3. Charles de Gaulle: Aster 15 alone.
findings.whatIsReal: All three are right, and the Horizon's "it carries Exocet from the first day, because a French warship without an anti-ship missile is not a thing that gets built" is both true and a good distinction against the Type 45. Charles de Gaulle really does carry Aster 15 and nothing heavier — 32 rounds in four Sylver A43 — so a lone SAM is the correct loadout, not an omission.
findings.fix: No change, except adding MdCN to corvette_f, which its own desc already promises.

findings.unit: missileboat (all eras), cruiser (e90 onward), ssgn (all eras)
findings.whatTheGameHas: All three slots empty, with the eras.js block comment stating why.
findings.whatIsReal: Every reason given is correct. The Marine Nationale has never commissioned a missile-armed fast attack craft, having built La Combattante by the dozen for export instead. Colbert decommissioned on 24 May 1991 and was the last cruiser any European navy in this game operates. MdCN is fired from a Suffren SSN's torpedo room, not from a dedicated missile boat. This is realism over symmetry working exactly as intended.
findings.fix: No change. Recorded as checked and sound.

findings.whatTheGameHas: NAVGUN deliberately carries no `fra` row, with a comment saying an era-less override would put a 1968 gun on every modern French hull and prescribing "put the CADAM on the era units' own weapons if it is wanted".
findings.whatIsReal: The reasoning is exactly right and the comment is the one piece of this subsystem that already understood the problem. Modern French escorts — Horizon, FREMM, FDI — really do mount the 76 mm Super Rapid, and the 100 mm Mle 68 CADAM really was correct only from 1968 to the 1990s. The fix below is that comment's own instruction carried out.
findings.fix: No change to NAVGUN. navgun_100_fr is authored outside /OTO 76mm/ so the loop cannot touch it.

findings.kind: service dates and the rows without one
findings.whatTheGameHas: All 23 era rows carry a `service` field; the four e20 rows carry none.
findings.whatIsReal: Checked every one against the real commissioning: 1954, 1955, 1955, 1956, 1951, 1964, 1962, 1967, 1959, 1961, 1986, 1976, 1974, 1980, (1986→)1961, 1997, 1996, 1988, 1963, 2017, 2012, 2010, 2001 — all correct for the named hull or lead ship. I also checked the four e20 rows that have NO service field, which an earlier audit reportedly skipped: POM (delivered 2023), FREMM (2012), Horizon (2010), Charles de Gaulle (2001) are all in commission today, so the absent field is the e20 convention and not an anachronism. Every era row is from:X to:X, so there is no hull surviving past its window.
findings.fix: No change except the fra_e80_carrier date that a duplicate key overwrites, reported above.

findings.whatTheGameHas: Le Fougueux 1954, La Combattante 1964, P400 1986, Flamant 1997, La Confiance 2017, Auguste Benebig 2023 — a constabulary line, all with `hmg`. La Fayette carries rcs 0.14, the lowest of any French hull.
findings.whatIsReal: All six identities, pennant numbers and dates are right, and the framing is right too: France has the second largest exclusive economic zone in the world, almost none of it in Europe, so its cheap hull is a colonial patrol vessel rather than a Baltic missile boat. La Fayette was the first warship in the world designed from the outset for a low radar signature, and 0.14 against a conventional hull's 0.6 says so.
findings.fix: No change.

edits.why: Author the French naval ordnance France actually built, so the era hulls stop firing American weapons. Placed in the existing "European naval ordnance" block immediately after asw_mu90, and named OUTSIDE the w_<era>_<fac>_<role> pattern so the era-range normaliser at the foot of generations.js leaves the figures alone, and outside /OTO 76mm/ so the NAVGUN substitution loop cannot touch them. Eleven weapons: two guns (127 mm Mle 1948 dual-purpose, 100 mm Mle 53/68 CADAM), three air-defence rounds on a deliberate ladder (Masurca area, Crotale EDIR point, Sadral last-ditch), two Exocet generations that are ANTI-SHIP ONLY because no Exocet before Block 3 could attack anything ashore, three anti-submarine weapons including Malafon which no other navy in the roster has an equivalent to, and MdCN — the only ship-launched land-attack cruise missile in Europe, with sea:0 because it has no anti-ship mode and manual:true following the release-authority rule already applied to the anti-radiation and ballistic rounds.

SEPARATING WHAT I MEASURED FROM WHAT I INFERRED.

MEASURED — everything below came out of jsc or python3 against the real files, never off a source line.

Harness: `var window=this;` + js/util.js js/config.js js/facts.js js/rules.js js/eras.js js/heavyair.js js/generations.js, run under /System/Library/Frameworks/JavaScriptCore.framework/Versions/A/Helpers/jsc. Every loadout in this report is the post-generations.js resolution, so the privateWeapon() clones and the DOMAIN `naval` scaling are already applied.

1. French surface inventory: 27 hulls with fac "fra" and layer "sea" — 23 era rows, 4 e20 rows. Full table in `inventory`, all fields read from the resolved objects.
2. Borrowed American ordnance: 18 of the 23 era hulls resolve a weapon whose base id matches /^w_e\d\d_nato_/. The five that do not are the patrol boats on the generic `hmg`. Zero era hulls carried a French-designed naval weapon.
3. Capability masks, baseline: of 27 French sea hulls, 13 could engage AIR, 1 could engage a SUBMARINE, 21 had ground:1 (almost all of that being naval gunfire, which is correctly land attack). After the proposed edits: 21 air, 7 sub, 23 ground.
4. MdCN: zero entries in WEAPONS match /mdcn|scalp|naval cruise/. Masurca, Malafon and Sadral likewise return nothing. The only "Crotale" in the table is w_e00_fra_spaag, the land-based Crotale NG VT-1.
5. Exocet: only corvette_f and destroyer_f (both e20) carried any Exocet-named weapon. No era hull did.
6. Shared-weapon blast radius, measured per id: w_e50_nato_cruiser on 3 hulls (nato/gbr/fra), w_e60_nato_cruiser on 3, w_e80_nato_corvette on 3, w_e80_nato_carrier on 3, w_e90_nato_destroyer on 4 (+deu), w_e00_nato_corvette on 4, w_e00_nato_destroyer on 4. This is why the fix points the French hulls at new French ids instead of editing the shared rows.
7. Mechanism confirmed by reading the code, not assumed: the era-range normaliser in generations.js gates on /^w_(e\d\d)_([a-z]+)_([a-z]+)$/ and only rewrites at/tankdestroyer/gunship/aa/spaag/mlrs/spg, so ids named outside that pattern are untouched. The NAVGUN loop only substitutes into weapons whose name matches /OTO 76mm/ and has no `fra` row by design. MISSILE_PROFILE and MISSILE_SPEED are applied with `if (WEAPONS[id])` guards, so new ids that declare profile/intercept/speed inline are fine. ui.js reads weapons[0] as the card's primary and lists the rest by name, which is why every proposed array puts the gun first.
8. `manual` gate read in entities.js line 485: `manualWeapon(w) { return !!(w && (w.manual || w.nuke || this.def.noAuto)); }` — per-weapon, so a FREMM holds MdCN while its gun, Aster and Exocet fire automatically. Confirmed at line 291 and 529 that the auto-acquire loops skip a manual weapon.
9. APPLIED AND RE-RESOLVED. I copied the repo to an isolated directory, applied all 21 edits with python3 assertions that every anchor had str.count == 1, rebuilt the bundle and re-ran jsc. Result: zero dangling weapon references anywhere in the roster (checked all 1,135 units, not just French ones).
10. COLLATERAL PROOF. I dumped every unit's resolved line (faction, name, sight, and every weapon's name/damage/range/accuracy/tgt mask) before and after, from ONE frozen snapshot, and diffed. Exactly 19 units changed and every one is French: corvette_f plus the 18 era rows. NON-French units changed: zero. Dangling refs after: zero.
11. BEHAVIOUR SUITE: 52 passed, 0 failed, "runtime errors: NONE", measured on a tree carrying the identical weapon block and the identical 18 loadout swaps. Two deltas have landed since that run — `manual:true` on mdcn, and the fra_e80_carrier duplicate-key collapse — and I could not re-run the suite to cover them (see risks). Both are verified behaviour-neutral under jsc: the carrier collapse produces byte-identical resolved name, full, service, desc and weapons, and `manual` only gates automatic target acquisition.
12. SIGHT SIDE EFFECT, measured not guessed. generations.js's "eyes to match the reach" pass raises a unit's sight to its longest non-arc weapon. Adding MdCN (range 19.0, resolving to 18.7 after the naval multiplier) lifts fra_e00_corvette's sight from 9.4 to 18.6 and corvette_f's from 14.8 to 18.6. For comparison I measured the existing convention: ssgn_n sits at sight 19.4 against tlam_n's 19.0, and every TEL sits at sight 24-31 against a 24-31 tile round. So this follows the game's own precedent, but it does make a FREMM the furthest-seeing surface ship in the roster.

THE LIVE REPO IS BEING EDITED CONCURRENTLY BY OTHER WORKFLOWS. I measured the unit count moving from 1,132 to 1,135 between two snapshots taken minutes apart, and the shared scratchpad root had my own working files overwritten by siblings twice. Every anchor in this report was re-verified with python3 str.count == 1 against the live js/rules.js and js/eras.js at the moment of writing, but re-verify each one before applying - especially if a submarine workflow has since touched the European naval ordnance block in rules.js, which is where the new weapons go.

MdCN LENGTHENS A FREMM'S EYES. generations.js derives sight from the longest non-arc weapon, so adding a 19-tile round lifts fra_e00_corvette from sight 9.4 to 18.6 and corvette_f from 14.8 to 18.6, making a French frigate the furthest-seeing surface ship in the game - a Nimitz is 12.9 and an Aegis destroyer 14.9. This matches the game's own precedent for commanded long-range missile carriers (ssgn_n sits at 19.4 against Tomahawk's 19.0; every TEL sits at 24-31), and `manual:true` stops the ship spending a thousand-kilometre round on the first patrol boat in range. But it is a real balance change and it deserves the owner's eye. If it is unwanted, shortening MdCN's range is the lever, not removing the weapon.

ELEVEN NEW WEAPON IDS, INCLUDING TWO EXTRA EXOCET GENERATIONS. Splitting Exocet into MM38 (1975, sea-only), MM40 Block 2 (1993, sea-only) and the existing MM40 Block 3 (2008, ground:1) is the honest answer to 'when could a French ship hit the shore', and it is the finding the owner asked for - but it adds rows to a table that already has roughly 1,700. If a smaller footprint is wanted, ssm_exocet38 alone would serve both e80 and e90 at the cost of the 42 km / 72 km distinction.

THE SHARED AMERICAN WEAPON ROWS ARE UNTOUCHED, DELIBERATELY. w_e50_nato_cruiser, w_e60_nato_cruiser, w_e80_nato_corvette, w_e90_nato_destroyer and the rest are still carried by the American, British and German hulls, and my collateral diff proves zero non-French units changed. But those rows have the same defects for their other carriers - a Type 22 is not an Oliver Hazard Perry either - and whoever owns the British and German surface fleets will hit the identical problem. The French fix is a template, not a system-wide repair.

TWO ROWS I DID NOT FIX AND SHOULD SAY SO. fra_e50_carrier (Arromanches, ~24 aircraft) and fra_e60_carrier (Clemenceau, ~40) still carry the shared 'Air wing of ~90 aircraft', which is a Forrestal's number. Correcting that text would move the American and British carrier rows too, so it is outside a France-only mandate and belongs to whoever owns the shared naval table.

fra_e80_aswhelo AND fra_e90_aswhelo carry asw_mk54 - the American Mk 54 of 2004 - on a French Lynx HAS Mk4 of 1979 and 1994. These are layer:'air' units and so strictly outside a surface-fleet brief, but they are the surface fleet's only anti-submarine aircraft for two decades and the correct round (asw_l5, or the existing asw_mu90) is to hand. Flagged rather than edited to avoid colliding with whoever owns the air roster.

THE TWO fra_e80_carrier EDITS ARE ORDER-DEPENDENT. Apply the identity edit first (it rewrites name, full, service and weapons together in one anchor), then the duplicate-key deletion. Applying them in the other order leaves the identity anchor unmatched.

THE NEW WEAPONS' NUMBERS ARE CALIBRATION, NOT MEASUREMENT. Damage, range, reload and accuracy were set by eye against neighbouring entries in the same tables so the air-defence ladder reads correctly (Masurca 9.8 / SM-1MR 10.4 / Aster 30 14.8 area, against Crotale 6.2 and Sadral 4.4 point). The dates, calibres, fits and target masks are history and should be defended; the numbers are game balance and should not be.
